pre_outcome_amendments.change: Finalize canonical low-FPR metric names and dataset-specific source-unit clusters before confirmatory probe training or evaluation.

title: A Probe Is Not a Monitor
primary_claim: Target-model decodability can remain high while layer selection, probe architecture, response policy, and operating thresholds fail to port.

estimands.baseline_reproducibility: Agreement with the paper under the paper model, data, feature site, probe, and evaluation protocol.
estimands.method_portability: Performance after retraining the published probe family on target-model activations.
estimands.selection_portability: Performance when the source layer or head selection rule is fixed before target-test evaluation.
estimands.operating_point_portability: Performance of development-frozen thresholds on target test data.
estimands.frozen_monitor_transfer: Reuse of learned source-probe parameters across models; not claimed by the current experiments.

primary_anchors.role: layer selection, probe-family ranking, and operating-point portability
response-policy, label-support, prompt-template, and normalization controls
nested head and layer selection under equal search budgets

supporting_evidence.role: identity-attribute decodability sanity check; not evidence for the unreproduced stereotype-personalization claim

layer_selection.sparse_grids: Frozen by each study-specific protocol; the root protocol does not override model-specific candidate layers.
layer_selection.dev_selected: Choose the layer maximizing the prespecified development aggregate within each training seed; evaluate it once on test.
layer_selection.oracle_test: Maximum test performance across candidates; diagnostic upper bound only and excluded from headline claims.

thresholds.name: dev_balanced_accuracy
thresholds.selection: maximize balanced accuracy on development data (equivalent to maximizing Youden J)

thresholds.name: dev_fpr_0.01
thresholds.selection: maximize development TPR subject to FPR <= 0.01

thresholds.name: dev_fpr_0.05
thresholds.selection: maximize development TPR subject to FPR <= 0.05

cluster_units.models-under-pressure: source prompt or document: Anthropic conversation index, ToolACE system/tool template, MT sample name, MTS original document ID, and released prompt ID for Mental Health and Aya
cluster_units.internal-instruction-following: task or instruction type, matching the held-out estimand
cluster_units.political-perspective: politician for congressional evaluation and document for news transfer

uncertainty.aggregation_rule: Aggregate within seed before across-seed inference; do not treat model-layer-dataset cells as independent.

confirmatory_holdouts.notes: Text backbone only; multimodal wrapper compatibility must be validated without inspecting task outcomes.
Standard causal-language-model interface; task outcomes remain untouched.

claim_rules: Previously inspected model results are retrospective reanalysis, not preregistered confirmation.
Only sealed model revisions evaluated after this freeze may be called prospective confirmatory holdouts.
Threshold-free test ROC operating points and performance at development-frozen thresholds are distinct metrics and must not be conflated.
Low-FPR outputs must retain negative-class count, false-positive count, achieved FPR, and empirical FPR resolution.
No study or condition may be removed because its result is positive, negative, or null.
Baseline failure, method-portability failure, selection-portability failure, and frozen-monitor failure are distinct outcomes.
Oracle test selection cannot support a generalization claim.
A cross-model difference requires uncertainty and a paired or nested comparison, not a raw point-estimate threshold.
Undefined metrics caused by single-class folds must be retained and reported as support failures.
All confirmatory outputs must retain row identifiers, labels, scores, probabilities, predictions, thresholds, seeds, and provenance.
